intent: To demonstrate the broad popularity of a gun licensing system among American voters, including those who live in households with firearms.

units.meaning: Among all American voters, 77% support the gun licensing system.

basis.note: Percent support among all American voters.

accepted_routes: 77% of all American voters support the gun licensing system.
Support among all American voters is 77%.
More than three-quarters (77%) of all American voters support it.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must visibly label the all-American-voters category with 77% or an equivalent text annotation.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause 'Ask all Americans, and more than three-quarters support it.'
units.reviewer_question: Is the overall 77% endpoint required, or can the clip convey only 'more than three-quarters'?

units.meaning: Among voters who Live in a house with a gun, 68% support the gun licensing system.

basis.entity: Live in a house with a gun
basis.note: Percent support among voters in gun households.

accepted_routes: 68% of voters who Live in a house with a gun support it.
Among gun-household voters, 68% think it is a good idea.
More than two-thirds (68%) of gun-household voters support it.
units.visual_evidence_rule: The chart must visibly label the 'Live in a house with a gun' category with 68% or an equivalent text annotation.
units.temporal_anchor: The clause 'Among voters who Live in a house with a gun...'
units.reviewer_question: Is the 68% gun-household endpoint required, or is the qualitative 'more than two-thirds' enough?

optional_valid: Both groups show majority support: 68% and 77% are both above 50%.
Gun-household support is lower than overall support but still high.
Both groups exceed the two-thirds threshold.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claims such as living with a gun causing lower or higher support.
Extrapolating beyond the table's groups, e.g., to non-voters or the general population not represented by the data.
Describing 68% as exactly two-thirds or 77% as exactly three-quarters.
Treating 68% and 77% as complementary shares of one whole or saying they sum to 100%.
Saying 77% of gun-household voters support it, or 68% of all voters support it.
Saying support is 9% higher rather than 9 percentage points higher.
Any time trend or change over time.
notes: The table gives two separate group percentages, not a composition; 68% and 77% are overlapping populations. The strongest required elements are the two endpoint figures plus the two explicit thresholds in the narration.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
